# rustinion_log_pipeline_processor (Resource)

Manages one stage of the Rustinion log processing/enrichment pipeline: a parse-and-enrich step run against every ingested log line before it is stored. Tenant-wide (no group_id) — bounded at 20 processors per tenant server-side.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Unique within the tenant.
- `processor_type` (String) One of: "grok_parse" (match a Grok pattern against the line's message and keep its named fields as attributes) or "remap" (rename an attribute an earlier processor produced).

### Optional

- `config` (String) The processor's config as a JSON string, shape depending on processor_type: grok_parse: {"pattern": "%{IPV4:client_ip} - %{HTTPMETHOD:method} %{URIPATH:path} %{INT:status:int}"}; remap: {"from": "status", "to": "http_status"}. A Grok pattern is a fixed grammar over a closed set of named patterns, never a raw regex — see the Log pipeline admin page for the supported pattern names. In an HCL string, write each `%{` as `%%{` (e.g. `jsonencode({ pattern = "%%{IPV4:client_ip}" })`); HCL otherwise reads `%{` as a template directive and rejects the config.
- `enabled` (Boolean)
- `position` (Number) Processors run in ascending position, so a remap can act on what an earlier grok_parse extracted. Ties are broken by creation time.
- `source_filter` (String) Restricts this processor to log lines whose source matches exactly. Omit to run it against every source.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
